chapter: Family, Margaret's story and Eutris's memories
title: Parades and the Knights of Pythias band
summary: They played only around the school; later he marched in the KP band down Seventh Avenue without reading music.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Just that one. And you used to go out, you say, on Auburn Avenue and play?
No, we didn't go that far. We just played around the school.
When he moved to Atlanta he used to step out at night.
We didn't go up and down the street or nothing like that. No parades or nothing like that. We couldn't play that well.
But they did have parades?
We never had no parades or nothing.
I'm just saying, but there were parades and things at that time?
Oh, yes, sure.
Did black people play in parades and things like that, at any festivities? Were there other black bands there, of older, more professional people, do you remember?
I'm sure there were because seems like I remember the Knights of Pythias - seemed like they had a band.
Who was that?
KP, they called it the KP band. That's the only thing I can remember, Knights of Pythias.
I played in that band; I forgot. I sure did, and couldn't read a note. Came all the way from Atlanta to New York and paraded down Seventh Avenue.
With the Knights of Pythias?
Yes.
That was after this time, though.
But you did that here?
Here, right here in New York.
Did you ever become a member of the lodge?

No, they tried to get me to but I was afraid, frightened. I thought they was going to beat me to death and all like that. They had a special meeting but I wouldn't accept it. They did take me in the band - well, I put the music up there but I couldn't read. We played marches and things like that and I couldn't read a note. We went all the way from Atlanta here to New York and we paraded down Seventh Avenue.
